candidate_relations.label: Acute Ischemic Stroke, left MCA territory
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms an acute ischemic stroke in the left MCA territory as a documented event, but the question asks for the most likely unifying diagnosis explaining the full constellation (bilateral orbital lesions, CSF pleocytosis/elevated protein, elevated inflammatory markers, pulmonary emboli, negative infectious/autoimmune/malignancy workup, negative SARS-CoV-2). The reference diagnosis is Primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS), of which the stroke is a manifestation. C001 names only the downstream ischemic event, not the underlying vasculitic etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: The left MCA territory infarct is a confirmed complication/manifestation of the underlying disease process, not the final unifying diagnosis requested

case_quality_flags: Atrial fibrillation and cardioembolic risk factors create diagnostic ambiguity; PACNS diagnosis rests on exclusion of alternative etiologies and supportive CSF/imaging findings
Bilateral orbital lesions and pulmonary emboli are atypical for classic PACNS and may warrant consideration of alternative systemic vasculitis or granulomatous disease despite negative screens
